<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**23** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bbed7ca5f41c3c4cd866f46b7d4dc89acc2cd7c4` — the merge of head `d6e1b7cab550e8058ee779debe7a2a3f9efbef94` into base `5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bbed7ca5f41c3c4cd866f46b7d4dc89acc2cd7c4 && git checkout bbed7ca5f41c3c4cd866f46b7d4dc89acc2cd7c4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11 d6e1b7cab550e8058ee779debe7a2a3f9efbef94 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11 && git merge --no-ff d6e1b7cab550e8058ee779debe7a2a3f9efbef94

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5fb79bc010cc9ab749dc29bfe44c83ef19f3dd11
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7198fc7ac668682f023ebce62b8e4a1f9fe4eb08`
Local-runs: probe — the brief asked for adversarial expressions judged at base and head: a scratch worktree of this head, `validateExpression` of merge-base `2f80f289` beside the head's, and `celEngine.evaluate` over four rows (served text, null, absent key, JS `Date`); plus the two changed test files (104 passed) and `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-date-text-call-refused.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/expression-refusal.ts, packages/formula/src/validate-date-text-arithmetic.test.ts, packages/formula/src/expression-refusal-codes.test.ts, the two declaration lines, the ADR-0087 marker and the frontmatter of .changeset/32595-date-text-call-refused.md + read, not reviewed: packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts, packages/formula/CHANGELOG.md (18.3.0, 51058ef), docs/adr/0053-date-and-datetime-semantics.md (D-F1), ruling 5507803003 on #13973, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-temporal.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-defaults-and-autonumbers.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- **The cited sources exist and say what the PR says.** On `origin/main` the `registerDateTextOverloads` docblock reads "ordering against another date field or a text literal → string-lex, and against a Timestamp → the text operand is coerced to a date: `bool`" and "`+` with text, or with another date field's text → string concatenation". `packages/formula/CHANGELOG.md` 18.3.0, 51058ef, Unchanged: "Date comparisons (`<`, `==`, against a literal, against `today()`), concatenation, `daysBetween` / `addDays`, number arithmetic, and a predicate that compares a duration … all stay accepted." ADR-0053 D-F1 and ruling 5507803003 (B1 narrow) both rule that the `@objectstack/driver-sql` read doors present `Field.datetime` and the audit stamps as canonical ISO-Z text and never a JS `Date`. `stdlib.ts` on main: `isoDate` refuses text "at build when the argument's type is known, at run otherwise".
- **Concatenation with text and ordering against a text LITERAL are covered** by that text. Measured base to head: `record.d + record.title` warning `type-mismatch` to clean; `record.d < '2026-12-01'` (fail-closed) error to clean; both evaluate to a value on the served row. Kept: `record.d < record.title`, a text field ordered against `record.at`, `record.flag + record.d`, `record.title < today()`, `'x' + (now() - record.at)`, and the `date-arithmetic` / `date-text-arithmetic` verdicts, each identical at base and head.
- **MUST-FIX 1 — the head accepts ordering shapes no published text names, so "Nothing is newly accepted" and `Clause-②: no` do not hold.** `ordersDateAgainstTextField` keeps the refusal only when the counterpart is a DIRECT text-field read. Any other text-valued operand goes clean. Measured at a fail-closed predicate, base `type-mismatch-fail-closed`, head clean:
  - `record.d < (record.flag ? record.title : record.other)` (a text FIELD, through a ternary)
  - `record.d < record.title + 'x'`
  - `record.d < upper(record.title)`
  - `record.d < string(record.amount)`
  - `record.d < isoDate(today())`

  The docblock names "another date field or a text literal"; the changelog names "against a literal, against `today()`". A computed text operand is neither. The PR's own rule for the text-field case ("no declared text covers it, so it keeps its refusal") is undone by one ternary around the same field. Fix, one of: (a) keep the base verdict for every ordering whose non-date operand is not a string literal, a date field or a Timestamp, and add those five rows to the double-judgment table as kept; or (b) declare the widening (`Clause-②: yes`) with its own declared text. (a) matches the claim.
- **SHOULD-FIX 2 — the narrowing is not limited to expressions that fault on every record.** The check reports a call wherever it sits. Measured base clean, head error, runtime answers a value:
  - `record.title == 'zzz' && isoDate(record.d) == '2026-11-01'` (fail-closed): `false` on every probed row, the call is never reached.
  - `record.d == null ? '' : isoDate(record.d)`: `''` on a null row.
  - `record.d != null && isoDate(record.d) == '2026-11-01'`: `false` on a null row.
  - `has(record.d) ? isoDate(record.d) : ''`: `''` on a row without the key.

  Refusing them is defensible, since the call faults whenever a served value reaches it and the prescribed rewrite keeps each guarded branch. But the ledger entry's `reason` ("the evaluator found no overload for the call on every record", "the refused shape faulted on every record, so no stored value depends on it") and the changeset's "That expression already read `null` or refused every write" are false for these. Word them as "on every record whose value reaches the call", and pin one guarded row in the table.
- **SHOULD-FIX 3 — "the runtime never holds a Timestamp there: every read door" is wider than its source.** D-F1 and the ruling govern `@objectstack/driver-sql`. Read on main: `driver-mongodb` stores `Field.datetime` as a BSON `Date` (`storageDatetimeValue`) and its source carries no text presentation on read; `validateRecord` accepts a JS `Date` on a date field from any writer by explicit decision (`engine-defaults-and-autonumbers.ts` docblock). With a `Date` bound, the refused calls evaluate today: `isoDate(record.d)` reads `"2026-11-01"`, `record.at.getHours()` reads `10`. Not run end to end here. The prescribed rewrite is safe on both shapes (`isoDate(date(record.at))` reads the same day on text and on a `Date`), so the prescription stands. Owed: measure the mongodb read door and a write-time validation rule handed a `Date`, then either scope the entry's wording to what was measured or record the reach.
- **The narrowing arm itself is real.** `isoDate(record.d)`, `isoDatetime(record.at)`, `record.at.getHours()`, `record.d.getFullYear()`, and the call inside a macro body (`[1,2].exists(i, record.at.getFullYear() == 2026 + i)`) are clean at base, refused at head, and fault on the served and the null row. Calls a string answers stay clean at both (`timestamp(record.at)`, `string`, `size`, `upper`, `contains`, `matches`, `in`, `daysBetween`, `addDays`, `addMonths`, `coalesce`). The residuals the PR names (`isoDate(coalesce(record.d, today()))`, `[record.at].all(x, x.getFullYear() == 2026)`, `dyn(record.at).getFullYear()`) are clean at both and fault at runtime: unchanged, no false refusal.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/formula` minor, `@objectstack/spec` patch. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` asks at least one moved package at `minor` or above; formula carries it, and the diff moves formula's published source. Spec moves one ledger entry and no accept set; both sit in one `fixed` group, so they version together. Correct per AGENTS.md step 3. No `major`.
- BREAKING banner, `!`, FROM/TO block and the one ADR-0087 marker are present. `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`: `registered formula-date-text-call-refused (new here)`, matching the entry `id`.
- The `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line is wrong while must-fix 1 stands.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author login is `os-sales` (relayed), not `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: read before landing.
- Implementing session on the PR body and dev report is `session_01L6bhgVZoYa8zU3KzZ3ht9P`; the reviewing seat session differs.
- Check-runs on this head at review time: Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset and every finished Lint / Type Check job `success`; `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`, Test Core and Test UI shards still `in_progress`. All-green is not yet in evidence.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #32818` is on the PR body; not checked here (prose face).
- Pre-existing, not this diff: `record.d.startsWith(record.title) && record.title < record.d` is clean at base and head though its second operand alone is refused. Card-worthy, not a finding on this PR.
- No security finding.

### ④ Design judgment

- `18.formula-date-text-call-refused.ts`: well-formed against `SemanticMigration` (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`), named and shaped like its sibling `18.formula-date-subtraction-refused.ts`, and semantic is the right kind: no mechanical rewrite exists for stored expressions. Its `replacement` is proven by the gate before it is prescribed and reads the right value on the card's rows. Against the card's acceptance (one type at authoring and at runtime; the card's rule and formula pinned) the narrowing makes the published `isoDate` contract real at build, which is "the spec's own refusal made real", not a declared capability taken away. The entry's `reason` carries the two overstatements of should-fix 2 and 3.
- `cel-engine.ts` `firstDateTextCall`: sound. It reads the fault off cel-js's structured code, judges each call on its own, and reports only a call whose `date(…)` rewrite checks clean. No false refusal found for a call a string answers.
- `cel-engine.ts` `confirmAgainstDateText` / `ordersDateAgainstTextField`: does not agree with the contract the PR declares (must-fix 1). The guard is spelled as "the counterpart is a text field read" where the declared text needs "the counterpart is a literal, a date field or a Timestamp".
- `validate.ts` `dateTextCallIssue`: agrees. It runs only where the date-text check found no arithmetic fault, so existing refusals keep their words; severity and outcome arms follow the date verdicts. The record-scope sentence "the field silently evaluates to null" is exact for a formula.
- `expression-refusal.ts`: five codes added to the closed set and the table, params typed. Additive.
- Tests: the double-judgment table is the right instrument and its rows hold. It has no row for an ordering against a computed text operand, which is how must-fix 1 passed, and no guarded row.
- Triage asked for the runtime to bind the declared type; the claim amendment moved the fix to the authoring side with the floor's reasoning recorded. That direction stands: binding a Timestamp would change expressions that read text today.

Findings: must-fix 1 (new acceptance beyond declared text; `Clause-②` line); should-fix 2 (guarded calls refused, "every record" wording in the ledger entry); should-fix 3 (premise wider than D-F1, mongodb and write-time `Date` unmeasured). No nit.
